description: OPEC adopted a production ceiling of 18.5 million barrels/day to halt the price slide from the 1986 crash
Iraq invaded Kuwait triggering the Gulf War, disrupting oil supply from the region
US-led coalition launched military operations against Iraq, causing oil supply uncertainty
Thai baht collapsed triggering a region-wide financial crisis that reduced Asian oil demand sharply
OPEC agreed to cut production by 1.245 million barrels/day alongside non-OPEC producers to stop price freefall
OPEC deepened cuts by a further 1.716 million barrels/day driving prices back above $15
Terrorist attacks in the US caused global economic uncertainty and initial demand shock
US-led coalition invaded Iraq removing a major oil producer from full capacity
Category 5 hurricane struck the US Gulf Coast disrupting ~27% of US oil production and refining capacity
Oil prices hit all-time high near $147/barrel driven by speculation and strong global demand

event: Lehman Brothers Collapse / Global Financial Crisis
description: Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy triggering the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression; oil demand collapsed
OPEC announced its largest ever single cut of 4.2 million barrels/day in response to the financial crisis
Uprising against Gaddafi regime disrupted Libyan oil production (~1.6 million barrels/day lost)
Rapid US shale oil production growth created a global supply glut before OPEC's November decision
OPEC decided NOT to cut production at its Vienna meeting signalling a market-share strategy against US shale
Iran nuclear agreement reached lifting sanctions and allowing Iranian oil back into global markets
Historic OPEC and non-OPEC agreement to cut production by 1.8 million barrels/day

event: US Withdrawal from Iran Nuclear Deal
description: US reimposed sanctions on Iran removing ~1.5 million barrels/day from global supply

event: Saudi-Russia Oil Price War / OPEC+ Collapse
description: Saudi Arabia and Russia failed to agree on production cuts; Saudi Arabia slashed prices and boosted output
WHO declared COVID-19 a global pandemic causing unprecedented collapse in oil demand
OPEC+ agreed to the largest ever production cut of 9.7 million barrels/day to stabilise markets
OPEC+ agreed to gradually increase production by 400000 barrels/day monthly from August 2021
Russia invaded Ukraine triggering Western sanctions and fears of Russian oil supply disruption

event: US Ban on Russian Oil Imports
description: US announced a ban on all Russian oil imports as part of sanctions over Ukraine invasion
OPEC+ agreed to cut production targets by 2 million barrels/day despite US pressure to increase supply
